record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How tightly is the semantic-subtyping approach tied to the presence of a type-case construct and explicit type annotations on values such as lambda-abstractions and channels? In particular, can semantic subtyping support useful languages without type-case, or any meaningful form of partial type reconstruction, while preserving the intended semantic distinctions and the model-based account of types?

evidence.quote: These observations make us wonder how much the semantic subtyping approach is bound to the presence of a type-case.

One may wonder if any form of partial type reconstruction is possible, and reformulate the previous question as whether the semantic subtyping approach is compatible with any form of type reconstruction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The semantic subtyping approach defines a subtyping relation on types by interpreting each type as a set of values and declaring s ≤ t whenever the interpretation of s is contained in that of t. This yields a set-theoretic account of unions, intersections, and negations of types, and is typically developed for languages featuring:
  (i) a type-case construct of the form "(x ∈ t) ? e1 : e2" that, at runtime, branches according to whether the value bound to x belongs to the type t, and
  (ii) explicit type annotations on values whose semantic type is not syntactically apparent — for instance, λ-abstractions annotated with their full intersection-of-arrows interface (λ^{⋂_i s_i → t_i} x. e) and communication channels annotated with the type of messages they carry.

These features are normally used in essential ways: the type-case is what gives observational meaning to fine-grained set-theoretic distinctions among types, and the annotations enable the model-based interpretation of values to be recovered from syntax (so that, e.g., a function annotated with Odd→Odd ∧ Even→Even is observably distinct from the same code annotated only with Int→Int).

Problem. Determine the extent to which the semantic-subtyping methodology is intrinsically tied to the presence of a type-case construct and to explicit type annotations on values such as λ-abstractions and channels. Concretely:

(a) Exhibit a useful programming language (e.g. a λ-calculus or process calculus with set-theoretic types including union, intersection, and negation) equipped with a semantic subtyping relation, in which there is no type-case construct, yet the semantic distinctions induced by the set-theoretic interpretation of types remain observable and the model-theoretic account of types is preserved; or prove that no such language exists, in the sense that without type-case the semantic-subtyping interpretation collapses to (or is indistinguishable from) a coarser, syntactic notion of subtyping.

(b) Determine whether the semantic-subtyping approach is compatible with any nontrivial form of (partial) type reconstruction — that is, a system in which type annotations on λ-abstractions and channels may be omitted (in whole or in part) and recovered by inference, while still admitting a sound and complete semantic interpretation of types as sets of values and preserving principal-type or minimum-typing-style properties.

Provide either constructions establishing the positive answers, or impossibility/lower-bound results delineating the precise dependence of semantic subtyping on type-case and on explicit annotations.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open challenge in the semantic-subtyping literature. Subsequent work (e.g., extensions of semantic subtyping with SMT-based decision procedures, logical approaches to deciding semantic subtyping, and various polymorphic extensions in the CDuce/set-theoretic types line) has refined decision procedures and added polymorphism, but no published result fully characterizes whether semantic subtyping can be sustained without a type-case construct or supports a general form of (partial) type reconstruction with set-theoretic types. The problem appears to remain open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Semantic subtyping: challenges, perspectives, and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists type-case dependence and type reconstruction as open challenges for the semantic-subtyping approach.
status_evidence.claim: Original framing of the problem as open.

status_evidence.title: Semantic Subtyping with an SMT Solver
status_evidence.snippet: Develops semantic subtyping decision procedures using SMT but retains type-case and explicit annotations.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work does not eliminate the dependence on type-case or provide full type reconstruction.

status_evidence.title: A Logical Approach To Deciding Semantic Subtyping
status_evidence.snippet: Focuses on deciding subtyping rather than removing type-case or enabling reconstruction.
status_evidence.claim: No reported resolution of the type-case-free or reconstruction-compatible variant.
